Germany's flash Composite Output Index rises to 53.8 in September from 51.8, marking an 11-month high and beating market expectations of 51.8.
Services PMI climbs to 52.9 from 49.7, a seven-month high, ending a five-month sequence of contraction, above the consensus of 50.
Manufacturing PMI falls to 53.8 from 54.3, also a two-month low, while remaining firmly above the 50 threshold, slightly below estimates.
Manufacturing Output Index eases to 55.9 from 56.6, a two-month low, but signals another solid increase in production.

"German businesses reported further signs of resilience in September, with output growth picking up speed, expectations towards the outlook holding steady, and employment rising for a second month running, all despite renewed pressure on the inflation front." said Phil Smith, Economics Associate Director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

title: Germany's business activity accelerates in September as services return to growth
